clauses.why: Server-side re-check of a chosen length cap protects nothing the bot's purpose needs; the page check already delivers the limit.
Exists only because the spec chose to persist conversations across sessions, which the request does not call for.
A labelled conversation list exists only because the spec added stored, multiple conversations.
Persisting conversations across sessions and logins is a capability beyond a working Grok chat bot.
Exists only because the spec chose to persist conversations across sessions, which the request does not call for.
A per-conversation storage cap only arises from the spec's own persistence feature.
A per-user conversation cap only arises from the spec's own persistence feature.
Conversation deletion with confirmation is a management feature of the added persistence.
Concerns the interaction of two added features, conversation deletion and the call log.
Exists only because the spec chose to persist conversations across sessions, which the request does not call for.
A truncation note is a refinement the request's purpose does not require; showing the returned text suffices.
An admin-editable settings store with an on/off switch is an operator feature the request does not ask for.
Validation of the added admin settings arises only from that extra feature.
Live settings changes arise only from the added configurable settings.
Access control for the added settings arises only from that extra feature.
The on/off switch and its behaviour are an operator feature not requested.
Server enforcement of the added on/off switch arises only from that extra feature.
In-flight behaviour of the added on/off switch arises only from that extra feature.
A call-log object with detailed fields is an audit feature the request does not call for.
Rules about the added call log arise only from that extra feature.
Content restrictions on the added call log arise only from that extra feature.
Access control for the added call log arises only from that extra feature.
Owner-only visibility of stored conversations arises only from the added persistence.
A permanent data-processing notice is a disclosure duty the request does not ask for.
Scheduled purging of logs and conversations exists only to manage the spec's added storage features.
The scheduling step for the added clean-up job arises only from that extra feature.
Preserving data and settings across redeployments is an operator lifecycle duty beyond creating the bot.
Rollback to earlier versions is a lifecycle capability the request does not call for.
Most listed README steps document added features: clean-up, key rotation, switch-off, rollback and storage limits.
Load-failure handling for the conversation list arises only from the added persistence.
The empty-list hint concerns the added conversation list.
Cross-tab consistency of a shared stored conversation arises only from the added persistence.
Race-safe re-checking of the added storage caps arises only from those extra limits.
Sending to a deleted conversation arises only from the added persistence and deletion.
Storage-failure handling of turns arises only from the added persistence.
Production-grade tests and coverage are not required to build a bot in a development org.
Duplicates server enforcement for refusals mostly tied to added features; access control is already covered by other clauses.
Portability to other orgs goes beyond the single development org requested.
In-flight isolation from settings and key changes arises from the added live settings and rotation features.
A separate administrator permission set exists only to govern the added settings and call log.
A notice about the added 90-day purge arises only from that extra feature.
Requiring that some applicable refusal appears adds nothing beyond the individual refusal clauses; which outcome appears is left unspecified.
